public_rationale: The claim bundles five abilities and gives no threshold for 'pretty poor'. One part is well supported. In November 2023, GPT-4 solved about a third of ConceptARC abstraction tasks while humans solved about 91%, a clear gap in flexible generalisation. GPT-4V also did badly on simple visual grids. The language-semantics part is contested: GPT-4 reached human-level scores on many language-heavy benchmarks, though whether those measure meaning is disputed. I found no 2023 human-versus-AI tests for world models, 3D navigation, or natural-scene comprehension. The record supports part of the bundle and leaves the rest unsettled, so I propose unresolved rather than supported or mixed.
limitations: Benchmarks are imperfect stand-ins for broad abilities like 'semantics' or 'world models'.
Only GPT-4-family systems were checked. Robotics and navigation systems were not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of November 2023, AI is still pretty poor at maintaining world models, inferring semantics from language, comprehending scenes, navigating the 3D world, and cognitive flexibility, where humans are good.

our_interpretation: Read as a claim about the best publicly evaluated AI systems in 2023 (for example GPT-4 and GPT-4V), compared with ordinary human performance.
'Pretty poor' is read as performance clearly and substantially below typical humans on tests built for that ability, not merely short of perfect.
The claim is a bundle of five abilities. It is fully supported only if all five show a clear gap. It is contradicted if several of them show AI at or near human level.
'As of today' names no period. I use 2023-01 to the post date of 2023-11-25, the period covered by evaluations of GPT-4-era systems published before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations from 2023 show the leading AI systems well below humans on each of the five named abilities: world models, language semantics, scene comprehension, 3D navigation, and cognitive flexibility.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations from 2023 show the leading AI systems at or near human level on most of the named abilities.

evidence.excerpt: However, GPT-4’s performance remains well below the high performance of humans, supporting the conclusion that, even with more informative prompting, the system lacks basic abstract reasoning abilities tested by this corpus.
evidence.explanation: In November 2023, GPT-4 solved 33% of ConceptARC tasks against about 91% for humans. This supports the 'cognitively flexible' part. It says nothing on its own about world models, 3D navigation, or language semantics.

evidence.excerpt: The visual one-shot prompt resulted in an accuracy of 0.23 over the 48 minimal tasks, compared with 0.69 for the (temperature 0) text-only counterpart.
evidence.explanation: GPT-4V did poorly on simple visual grid tasks that humans solve about 95% of the time. This bears loosely on visual comprehension, but abstract grids are not natural scenes.

evidence.excerpt: While less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports human-level scores on many language-heavy exams. This cuts against a plain reading that AI was 'pretty poor' at getting meaning from language. Whether exam scores measure semantic understanding is itself disputed.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Human-versus-AI evaluations from 2023 on world-model tracking, 3D navigation, and natural-scene understanding, plus an agreed reading of what counts as 'pretty poor' at semantics.
